workflow: A mutable in-memory buffer begins a write-like operation and validates that its internal storage is usable.
Acquiring the caller-provided input invokes user-controlled code that re-enters the same buffer and closes or otherwise mutates it.
The re-entrant mutation releases or invalidates the internal storage while the outer operation continues.
The outer operation fails to revalidate the buffer state and writes through the stale storage, causing use-after-free and process termination instead of a recoverable mutation or-간
summary: Reentrant mutation invalidates backing storage before write completion
decision_reason: The underlying failure workflow materially matches the existing cluster: user-controlled conversion/acquisition code mutates or detaches a backing resource, and the outer operation continues without revalidating it before later use. The specific symptom here is use-after-free of internal buffer data
